Wisell, T., Jerksjo, M., Hult, C. (IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute) and Lindgren, M. (Swedish Transport Administration) (2018). Fuel and Technology Alternatives in Non-Road Engines. IEA Advanced Motor Fuels TCP, Annex 50.

BACKGROUND ONLY - no extraction. What it is and why no data: Non-road mobile machinery (agricultural tractors and construction equipment): emission standards, NOx/PM/HC/CO emission factors (g/kWh) from on-board testing, retrofit after-treatment, inventory models and policy. Almost all numbers are non-GHG pollutants (out of scope); fuel consumption is discussed but no per-machine fuel use per unit of work or cost is printed. Checked against mobile-equipment_* and haul-truck_* archetypes: nothing loadable. Year from PDF metadata (June 2018); cover has no date. What it does have: Claims (reprinted, not loaded): battery-electric underground loader (Atlas Copco Scooptram ST7, 2016) energy use about 80% below diesel (p.49, 51); Volvo CE/Skanska electric quarry project aiming at up to 95% lower carbon emissions and 25% lower total cost of ownership, energy use projected 70% lower (pp.48-51); dual-fuel (biogas-diesel) tractors about 40% lower climate impact than diesel, methane 15-30% of first-generation climate impact (p.43). Could support mobile-equipment_battery-electric or haul-truck_battery-electric only as manufacturer claims.
